title: BevacizuMAV : Evaluation of the efficacy and safety of anti-angiogenic treatment with intravenous bevacizumab in patients with symptomatic cerebral arteriovenous malformations
official: BevacizuMAV : Evaluation of the efficacy and safety of anti-angiogenic treatment with intravenous bevacizumab in patients with symptomatic cerebral arteriovenous malformations
summary: Main objective: Evaluate the 6-month efficacy of IV injections of bevacizumab 5mg/kg every 14 days for 3 months (6 injections) on disabling symptoms in patients with symptomatic cerebral arteriovenous malformations ineligible for interventional therapy.

interventions.name: Abevmy 25 mg/mL concentrate for solution for infusion.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patient over 18 years
2. Affiliated or beneficiary of a social security plan
3. With a symptomatic cerebral AVM (chronic headache, focal neurological deficit, cognitive impairment, epilepsy) of Spetzler and Martin grade III, IV or V
4. Whose symptoms are sufficiently severe to allow significant improvement with treatment: MoCA score ≤ 25 and/or ; NIHSS score ≥ 4 and/or ; Epilepsy Balance Score ≥ 2 and/or ; HIT-6 score ≥ 48
5. With functional signs and symptoms not sequellar to a previous bleeding episode AND disabling (mRS>1)
6. Ineligible for therapeutic intervention (endovascular or neurosurgery or radiosurgery)
7. With normal bone marrow, liver and kidney function
8. For women of childbearing potential: negative pregnancy test within 14 days prior to inclusion and effective contraception for up to 6 months after the end of treatment
9. Fluency in the french language
10. Having received informed consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
1. Known allergy to bevacizumab or an excipient
2. Patient under legal protection
3. Pregnant or breast-feeding women
4. Hypersensitivity to Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cell products or other recombinant human or humanized antibodies
5. Contraindication to cerebral MRI (claustrophobia, pacemaker or other implantable device contraindicating MRI)
6. Absolute or relative contraindication to gadolinium injection (history of true allergic reaction or intolerance to gadobutrol, renal failure with creatinine clearance <15mL/min, pregnant or breast-feeding woman)
7. Proteinuria ≥ 2+ on urine dipstick (patients with proteinuria ≥2+ on urine dipstick will need to have proteinuria ≤ 1g protein on 24-hour urine to be eligible)
8. Uncontrolled hypertension (PAS >150 and/or PAD > 100 mmHg)
9. History of hypertensive crisis or hypertensive encephalopathy
10. Congestive heart failure (New York Heart Association Grade II or higher)
11. Previous myocardial infarction or unstable angina in the preceding 12 months
12. Symptomatic peripheral vascular disease
13. Patient with balanced blood pressure on quadritherapy
14. Patients with severe coronary artery disease or recent ACS
15. Vascular disease (aortic aneurysm, aortic dissection)
16. Major surgery, open biopsy or significant traumatic lesion within 4 weeks prior to inclusion, or anticipation of need for major surgery during study period
17. Biopsy or other minor surgical procedure, excluding placement of a vascular access device, within 7 days prior to inclusion
18. History of abdominal fistula, gastrointestinal perforation or intra-abdominal abscess within 6 months of inclusion
19. Significant unhealed wound, ulcer or bone fracture
20. Thrombotic episode within 6 months prior to inclusion
21. Atrial fibrillation
